claims: C1: honoring a user request is permitted when it does not conflict with a developer-, system-, or root-level instruction
C2: honoring a user request is forbidden when it conflicts with a developer-, system-, or root-level instruction

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: the level of instruction authority held by instructions from end users

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: user_request
concepts.gloss: R is a request made by an end user
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of honoring user requests, so a class of user requests must exist

concepts.name: higher_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction at the developer, system, or root level of the authority hierarchy

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: request R and instruction I direct incompatible behavior
concepts.inference: the clause's exception turns on a conflict between a user request and a higher-level instruction; which pairs conflict is a fact about the case

ontology.gloss: I is an instruction at the developer, system, or root level of the authority hierarchy

asserts.read_back: honoring user request % is permitted because it does not conflict with any developer-, system-, or root-level instruction
asserts.body: user_request(R), not higher_level_instruction(I), not conflicts_with(R, I)

asserts.read_back: honoring user request % is forbidden because it conflicts with developer-, system-, or root-level instruction %

closure.reason: the clause states that user requests should be honored unless they conflict with higher-level instructions; silence about other cases leaves them permitted

checks.evidence: Models should honor user requests unless they conflict with developer-, system-, or root-level instructions.
checks.action: The clause's default is to honor user requests; the exception is a conflict with higher-level instructions. The permit rule covers the default, and the forbid rule covers the exception.
